This word means 'bread' and represents not only physical food but also the symbol of life and communion. In Jewish culture, bread is a central element of meals and religious rituals. In this verse, it takes on a spiritual dimension, announcing the bread of life that Jesus is for humanity, thus illustrating divine provision.

This term means 'many' or 'numerous', and it emphasizes abundance. In the context of this miracle, it highlights the large crowd that needs food, but also Jesus' ability to provide abundantly. Spiritually, this reminds us that God is capable of meeting all our needs, even when resources seem insufficient.

36.epoque: This account is set in the first century, during Jesus' ministry in Galilee, a period marked by Roman occupation and intense messianic expectation among the Jewish people.
36.passage: Matthew 15 discusses the teachings of Jesus and his miracles, including the multiplication of the loaves, which illustrates his compassion for the hungry crowd and his divine power. This chapter also shows the tension between religious traditions and the truth revealed by Jesus.
36.culture: In Jewish culture, a meal is a sacred act that symbolizes communion and community. Bread, in particular, is a symbol of God's provision, recalling the manna in the desert.
36.interpretation: This verse illustrates how Jesus takes what is limited (seven loaves and a few fish) and transforms it into an abundance that satisfies the needs of all. This reminds us that even our limited resources, when offered to God, can be used to accomplish miracles.
36.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of gratitude and dependence on God for our needs. By giving thanks before distributing the loaves, Jesus shows us that recognition is essential in our relationship with God. We are called to entrust our small resources to him, for he can multiply them to bless others.

mots.sens: This term primarily refers to bread, a staple food in the diet of people at the time. In a broader sense, it symbolizes God's provision for His creatures. Theologically, this evokes humanity's dependence on God for both spiritual and physical sustenance, reminding us that Jesus is the 'bread of life' who satisfies the deepest needs of the soul.

This verb means 'to be filled' or 'to complete.' It emphasizes the idea of fullness and satisfaction. In the context of this verse, it illustrates God's generosity in abundantly providing for those who follow Him, reinforcing the notion that divine grace leaves nothing lacking.

This word refers to a basket, often used to carry food. In this passage, it represents not only the abundance of leftovers but also how God cares for His children by providing more than they need. This underscores the idea that God's blessing overflows and that nothing is lost of what He gives.

37.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Jesus' ministry in Galilee during the 1st century, a period marked by messianic expectations and religious tensions between the Jews and Roman authorities.
37.passage: In Matthew 15, Jesus teaches and heals the crowds, and this verse is part of the account of the multiplication of the loaves, illustrating Jesus' compassion for the hungry crowds. This miracle demonstrates His divine authority and His ability to meet the physical and spiritual needs of the people.
37.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, sharing food was an act of hospitality and communion. The multiplication of the loaves goes beyond merely satisfying material needs; it creates a space of community and sharing among people.
37.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that Jesus is the one who meets the needs of humanity. The abundance of leftovers symbolizes God's overflowing grace, which is not limited to immediate satisfaction but also offers blessings that endure and multiply.
37.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God abundantly provides for our needs, both material and spiritual. As believers, we are called to trust in His provision and to share generously with those around us. The multiplication of the loaves also reminds us that even in our most desperate situations, God can act miraculously to nourish and restore us.

mots.sens: This word means 'men' or 'human beings' and is often used in the New Testament to refer to humanity as a whole. It emphasizes the dignity and value of each individual, created in the image of God. In this verse, it highlights the fact that Jesus addresses a group of people, reinforcing the idea that His ministry touches all aspects of human life.

This term means 'to eat' and refers to the action of consuming food. In the context of this miracle, it evokes not only the physical need for food but also the satisfaction that Jesus brings to those who follow Him. This underscores the importance of Jesus as the provider who meets our material and spiritual needs.

38.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Jesus' ministry in the 1st century in Galilee, where He teaches and performs miracles, attracting large crowds.
38.passage: Matthew 15 recounts the miracle of the multiplication of the loaves, where Jesus feeds a large crowd with few resources, illustrating His divine power and compassion for the people.
38.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, sharing food was an act of communion and solidarity. Feeding a crowd was a sign of generosity and kindness, values highly esteemed in Jewish society.
38.interpretation: This verse highlights Jesus' ability to meet the physical needs of people while also symbolizing His spiritual provision. The mention of 'four thousand men' without including women and children may also indicate the importance of community and family in Jesus' ministry.
38.commentaire: This miracle reminds us that Jesus cares about our needs, whether material or spiritual. As believers, we are called to trust in His provision and to share with those in need, just as Jesus did. It also encourages us to see each person as precious in God's eyes, worthy of His attention and grace.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to release' or 'to send away.' It evokes the idea of ending an obligation or relieving pressure. In this context, Jesus sends the crowd away after meeting their spiritual and physical needs, illustrating His authority and compassion. It also emphasizes that Jesus is the one who brings deliverance and peace.

This term refers to a 'boat' or 'ship.' It refers to the means of maritime transport used at the time, often associated with crossing water. In the biblical context, the boat often symbolizes a journey of faith or a spiritual transition, reminding us that the disciples and Jesus often face storms and challenges along their path.

Magadan is a place mentioned in the New Testament, often identified as a coastal region. Its name evokes connotations of wealth and abundance, which can be interpreted as a symbol of divine provision. The mention of this region underscores Jesus' ministry that extends beyond usual boundaries, reaching places of spiritual need.

39.epoque: The passage is set in the 1st century during Jesus' earthly ministry, a period marked by political and religious tensions in Israel under Roman occupation.
39.passage: This verse concludes an episode where Jesus fed a large crowd, demonstrating His power and compassion. Chapter 15 addresses themes of purity, tradition, and the true nature of the human heart.
39.culture: At the time, crowds followed Jesus not only for His teachings but also for His miracles, reflecting a quest for signs and wonders. The boat also symbolizes trade and travel, essential in Mediterranean culture.
39.interpretation: Jesus sends the crowd away after meeting their needs, showing that He is the provider of all we need. His ascent into the boat to go to Magadan symbolizes a new chapter in His ministry, where He continues to teach and heal.
39.commentaire: This verse reminds us that Jesus is always on the move, calling us to follow Him in our own journey of faith. He teaches us the importance of sometimes withdrawing to recharge while remaining attentive to the needs of others. By sending the crowd away, He shows us that our mission is to share God's love and grace with those around us.
